description: Reaction energies of molecules adsorbing on metal and oxide surfaces, against experiment: ADS41 (Sharada et al., Phys. Rev. B 100, 035439 (2019), Table I) and Surf13 (Shi et al., Nat. Chem. 17, 1688 (2025)). Built by scripts/build_adsorption_dataset.py; energies in eV, lengths in Å.

MgO(001) 2x2.note: a layer is a conventional cell (two atomic layers): four atomic layers, the bottom two fixed

TiO2 rutile(110) p(4x2).note: a layer is an O-Ti-O trilayer; x along [-110], y along [001] (the rows of five-fold Ti)

TiO2 anatase(101) 3x1.note: a layer is an O-Ti-O block (12 atoms per surface cell); x along [10-1], y along [010]

CO/Co(0001) ontop.configuration: CO upright on the ontop site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. (2022) Table 3); C-Co 1.75 Å.

CO/Cu(111) ontop.configuration: CO upright on the ontop site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. (2022) Table 3); C-Cu 1.85 Å.

CO/Ir(111) ontop.configuration: CO upright on the ontop site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. (2022) Table 3); C-Ir 1.86 Å.

CO/Ni(111) fcc.configuration: CO upright on the fcc site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. (2022) Table 3); C-Ni 1.95 Å.

CO/Pd(100) bridge.configuration: CO upright on the bridge site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. (2022) Table 3); C-Pd 1.98 Å.

CO/Pd(111) fcc.configuration: CO upright on the fcc site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. (2022) Table 3); C-Pd 2.07 Å.

CO/Pt(111) ontop.configuration: CO upright on the ontop site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. (2022) Table 3); C-Pt 1.85 Å.

CO/Rh(111) ontop.configuration: CO upright on the ontop site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. (2022) Table 3); C-Rh 1.83 Å.

CO/Ru(0001) ontop.configuration: CO upright on the ontop site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. (2022) Table 3); C-Ru 1.92 Å.

NO/Pd(100) hollow.configuration: NO upright on the hollow site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1, systems 11-13; Araujo et al. Table 3); N-Pd 2.15 Å.

NO/Pd(111) fcc.configuration: NO upright on the fcc site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1, systems 11-13; Araujo et al. Table 3); N-Pd 2.05 Å.

NO/Pt(111) fcc.configuration: NO upright on the fcc site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1, systems 11-13; Araujo et al. Table 3); N-Pt 2.07 Å.

H/Ni(100) hollow 2x2.configuration: H on the hollow site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. Table 3); H-Ni 1.85 Å.

H/Ni(111) fcc 2x2.configuration: H on the fcc site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. Table 3); H-Ni 1.71 Å.

H/Pd(111) fcc 2x2.configuration: H on the fcc site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. Table 3); H-Pd 1.80 Å.

H/Pt(111) fcc 2x2.configuration: H on the fcc site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. Table 3); Araujo et al. list the top site, but Fig. S1 (system 18) shows H in a three-fold hollow; H-Pt 1.86 Å.

H/Rh(111) fcc 2x2.configuration: H on the fcc site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. Table 3); H-Rh 1.85 Å.

I/Pt(111) fcc 2x2.configuration: I on the fcc site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. Table 3); I-Pt 2.75 Å.

N/Ni(100) hollow 2x2.configuration: N on the hollow site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. Table 3); N-Ni 1.85 Å.

O/Ni(100) hollow 2x2.configuration: O on the hollow site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. Table 3); O-Ni 1.96 Å.

O/Ni(111) fcc 2x2.configuration: O on the fcc site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. Table 3); O-Ni 1.86 Å.

O/Pt(111) fcc 3x3.configuration: O on the fcc site at 1/9 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. Table 3); O-Pt 2.05 Å.

O/Rh(100) hollow 2x2.configuration: O on the hollow site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1; Araujo et al. Table 3); O-Rh 2.08 Å.

H/Pt(111) fcc 3x3.configuration: H on the fcc site at 1/9 ML, the 3x3 slab of the ethylene dissociation (Sharada et al. (2019) Appendix A).

CCH3/Pt(111) fcc 3x3.configuration: Ethylidyne on the fcc site at 1/9 ML, C-C along the normal (Sharada et al. Appendix A: 3x3 slab); C-Pt 2.00 Å, C-C 1.50 Å.

CH/Pt(111) fcc 4x4.configuration: Methylidyne on the fcc site at 1/16 ML (Araujo et al., to mimic the low coverage of the experiment; CE39 used 1/4 ML); C-Pt 2.02 Å.

CH3/Pt(111) ontop 4x4.configuration: Methyl on the top site (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1, system 27) at 1/16 ML (Araujo et al.; CE39 used 1/4 ML); C-Pt 2.08 Å.

CH3I/Pt(111) ontop.configuration: CH3I standing on I on the top site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1, system 25); I-Pt 2.80 Å.

CH3OH/Pt(111) ontop.configuration: CH3OH bound through O on the top site at 1/4 ML, C-O tilted 45° from the normal and the hydroxyl H near the surface plane (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1, system 26); O-Pt 2.40 Å.

CH4/Pt(111) fcc.configuration: CH4 over the fcc site at 1/4 ML with three H down (tripod, Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1 system 28; site: Araujo et al. Table 3); the lower H 2.60 Å above the top layer.

NH3/Cu(100) ontop.configuration: NH3 bound through N on the top site at 1/4 ML (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1, system 24); N-Cu 2.10 Å.

C2H6/Pt(111) fcc.configuration: Ethane at 1/9 ML with its C-C axis parallel to the surface along [2a1 - a2] (as in Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1, system 29), the C-C midpoint over the fcc site (Araujo et al. Table 3); the lowest H 2.50 Å above the top layer.

C3H8/Pt(111) ontop.configuration: All-trans C3H8 at 1/9 ML lying flat, its carbon plane parallel to the surface and the chain along a close-packed row (as in Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1, systems 30-31), the carbon centroid over a top site (Araujo et al. Table 3); the lowest H 2.50 Å above the top layer.

C4H10/Pt(111) ontop.configuration: All-trans C4H10 at 1/9 ML lying flat, its carbon plane parallel to the surface and the chain along a close-packed row (as in Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1, systems 30-31), the carbon centroid over a top site (Araujo et al. Table 3); the lowest H 2.50 Å above the top layer.

C6H6/Cu(111) fcc.configuration: Benzene at 1/9 ML lying flat over the fcc site, two C-H bonds along y (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1, systems 33-35; site: Araujo et al. Table 3); the ring 3.0 Å above the top layer.

C6H6/Ag(111) fcc.configuration: Benzene at 1/9 ML lying flat over the fcc site, two C-H bonds along y (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1, systems 33-35; site: Araujo et al. Table 3); the ring 3.1 Å above the top layer.

C6H6/Au(111) fcc.configuration: Benzene at 1/9 ML lying flat over the fcc site, two C-H bonds along y (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1, systems 33-35; site: Araujo et al. Table 3); the ring 3.1 Å above the top layer.

C6H6/Pt(111) bridge.configuration: Benzene at 1/9 ML chemisorbed over the bridge site, in the geometry relaxed by Araujo et al. (2022) on a five-layer slab with four relaxed layers (their SI Supplementary Note 1; CE39 used a flat benzene on a four-layer slab).

C6H10/Pt(111) bridge.configuration: Cyclohexene at 1/9 ML di-sigma bonded through C1 and C2 over a bridge site, the ring rising at 50° from the surface (Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1, system 36), on the five-layer slab with four relaxed layers of Araujo et al.; C1 and C2 2.00 Å above the top layer, their H atoms in sp3 positions.

C10H8/Pt(111) ontop.configuration: Naphthalene at 1/16 ML (4x4 slab, Sharada et al. Appendix A) lying flat, the molecule centred over a top site with the long axis along a close-packed row, so that both rings sit next to bridge sites (the di-bridge geometry, the most stable of Morin et al., J. Phys. Chem. B 108, 12084 (2004)); the carbons 2.10 Å above the top layer, the C-H bonds bent 20° up.

(H2O)6/Pt(111).configuration: Water at 2/3 ML as the hexagonal H-down bilayer (Araujo et al. (2022), as in the experiment's islands; CE39 used a single molecule at 1/4 ML): O atoms on the top sites of a honeycomb, three flat-lying molecules (O 2.30 Å above Pt) donating two H bonds and three molecules 0.8 Å higher donating one and pointing the other H down; 6 H2O per 3x3 cell.

(H2O...OH)3/Pt(111).configuration: The flat (H2O...OH) honeycomb of Wellendorff et al. (2015) SI Fig. S1, system 39: O atoms on the top sites, H2O and OH alternating, every H in an H bond (3 H2O + 3 OH per 3x3 cell, 2/3 ML).

O/Pt(111) fcc 3x2.configuration: O on the fcc site at 1/6 ML: the O coverage consumed by the (H2O...OH) network of the 3x3 cell (1.5 O per 9 Pt, Wellendorff et al. Table 3); O-Pt 2.05 Å.

CH4/MgO(001).configuration: CH4 over Mg with two H down (dipod): the relaxed revPBE-D4 geometry of Shi et al. (2025) (Data_autoSKZCAM, Data/04-Molecule_Surface/MgO/CH4), placed relative to a surface Mg.

C2H6/MgO(001).configuration: ethane lying nearly flat over Mg: the relaxed revPBE-D4 geometry of Shi et al. (2025) (Data_autoSKZCAM, Data/04-Molecule_Surface/MgO/C2H6), placed relative to a surface Mg.

CO/MgO(001).configuration: CO upright on Mg, C down: the relaxed revPBE-D4 geometry of Shi et al. (2025) (Data_autoSKZCAM, Data/04-Molecule_Surface/MgO/CO), placed relative to a surface Mg.

CO2/MgO(001) chemisorbed.configuration: CO2 chemisorbed as a carbonate on a surface O, its O atoms towards two Mg (the state Shi et al. assign to the experiment of Chakradhar and Burghaus; Surf13 holds the physisorbed state): the relaxed revPBE-D4 geometry of Shi et al. (2025) (Data_autoSKZCAM, Data/04-Molecule_Surface/MgO/CO2_Chemisorbed), placed relative to a surface O.

H2O/MgO(001).configuration: H2O monomer on Mg, one H bond to surface O: the relaxed revPBE-D4 geometry of Shi et al. (2025) (Data_autoSKZCAM, Data/04-Molecule_Surface/MgO/H2O_Monomer), placed relative to a surface Mg.

N2O/MgO(001).configuration: N2O lying parallel to the surface: the relaxed revPBE-D4 geometry of Shi et al. (2025) (Data_autoSKZCAM, Data/04-Molecule_Surface/MgO/N2O_Parallel), placed relative to a surface Mg.

NH3/MgO(001).configuration: NH3 on Mg, N down: the relaxed revPBE-D4 geometry of Shi et al. (2025) (Data_autoSKZCAM, Data/04-Molecule_Surface/MgO/NH3), placed relative to a surface Mg.

CH4/TiO2 rutile(110).configuration: CH4 over a five-fold Ti, two H down: the relaxed revPBE-D4 geometry of Shi et al. (2025) (Data_autoSKZCAM, Data/04-Molecule_Surface/r-TiO2/CH4), placed relative to a five-fold Ti.

CO2/TiO2 rutile(110) tilted.configuration: CO2 tilted, one O on a five-fold Ti: the relaxed revPBE-D4 geometry of Shi et al. (2025) (Data_autoSKZCAM, Data/04-Molecule_Surface/r-TiO2/CO2_Tilted), placed relative to a five-fold Ti.

H2O/TiO2 rutile(110).configuration: H2O on a five-fold Ti, one H bond to a bridging O: the relaxed revPBE-D4 geometry of Shi et al. (2025) (Data_autoSKZCAM, Data/04-Molecule_Surface/r-TiO2/H2O), placed relative to a five-fold Ti.

CH3OH/TiO2 rutile(110).configuration: CH3OH bound through O to a five-fold Ti, H bond to a bridging O: the relaxed revPBE-D4 geometry of Shi et al. (2025) (Data_autoSKZCAM, Data/04-Molecule_Surface/r-TiO2/CH3OH), placed relative to a five-fold Ti.

H2O/TiO2 anatase(101).configuration: H2O on a five-fold Ti, H atoms towards two-fold O: the relaxed revPBE-D4 geometry of Shi et al. (2025) (Data_autoSKZCAM, Data/04-Molecule_Surface/a-TiO2/H2O), placed relative to a five-fold Ti.

NH3/TiO2 anatase(101).configuration: NH3 on a five-fold Ti, N down: the relaxed revPBE-D4 geometry of Shi et al. (2025) (Data_autoSKZCAM, Data/04-Molecule_Surface/a-TiO2/NH3), placed relative to a five-fold Ti.
